newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Australian 10-yr bond stays at lofty level.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Australian 10-yr bond stays at lofty level.

text.p: *Australian 10-year bond futures stayed close to 3-1/2 year highs in SYCOM, but with the contract overbought and a 1/2 point rate cut factored in, the advance from here could be tempered.
*All eyes on RBA at 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) after Thursday's disappointing labour force data buoyed easing expectations.

The September Australian 10-year bond futures stayed close to 3-1/2 year highs in SYCOM, but with the contract overbought and a 1/2 point official rate cut factored in, the advance from here could be tempered.

The contract ended after hours trade at 93.365, up slightly from a 93.360 pit close, and still within a whisker of Thursday's intra-day peak of 93.415 which followed a disappointing labour force report for June.
Peter Pontikis, technical strategist at Westpac, said he would regard moves into high 93.300s to 93.410 as selling opportunites.
"(The contract) is technically overbought...with risk/reward ratio of fresh longs very poor," Pontikis said, adding that he would prefer to sell into strength now.

The contract is well into overbought territory with a relative strength index at over 80 percent as the market continues an advance from 92.825 since late June and as part of a larger uptrend from 91.700 at the start of April.

September bill futures ended SYCOM at 93.95, after rushing to a contract high of 94.99 in immediate response to Thursday's weaker than expected employment report, equating to a cash rate of 5.05 percent against official rates of 5.5 percent.

The data has put the market on alert for an easing in policy by the Reserve Bank, even as early as 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) today, although there is a feeling it would be more likely after the inflation and wages data later this month.
Meanwhile, U.S. Treasuries ended Thursday's session little changed ahead of the June U.S. PPI later on Friday.
